name: Field Trace
intent: A campus wayfinding interface expressed as an authoritative working field plan, with the map as the dominant surface.

typography.displayFamily: Fira Sans Condensed, Segoe UI, sans-serif

motion.reducedMotion: Disable non-essential transitions and preserve immediate state feedback.

desktopPlanning.layout: Slim ruled planner on the left, dominant central map, vertical eight-floor binding on the right, and utility controls above.

desktopActiveRoute.layout: Planner transforms into route status and instructions while the map stays dominant; next physical action remains fully readable.

mobilePlanning.layout: Horizontal floor binding, route setup, then a zoomable and pannable map.

mobileActiveRoute.layout: Compact route summary followed by a closer map with a fixed bottom next-action tray.
mobileActiveRoute.details: Collapsed by default and accessible through an explicit Route details toggle.
mobileActiveRoute.map: Zoomed for relevant room and facility labels while retaining pan and zoom controls.
mobileActiveRoute.bottomReserve: Reserve layout space equal to the fixed tray height so content is not obscured.

componentGuidance.map: Primary visual surface with measured grid, floor-plan geometry, route trace, current-position marker, and technical annotations.
componentGuidance.planner: Ruled working sheet, not a card stack; form controls align to a compact field-note rhythm.
componentGuidance.floorBinding: Always represents all eight floors; vertical on desktop and horizontal on mobile.
componentGuidance.controls: Square technical construction, direct labels, visible focus, and no decorative gradients.
componentGuidance.nextActionTray: Shows the complete next instruction and preserves I’m here and Blocked actions without truncation.

guardrails: Do not turn the interface into a generic dashboard or card grid.
Do not add gradients, glassmorphism, oversized corner radii, or decorative elevation.
Do not let route detail displace the active map from the first mobile viewport.
Do not use orange or teal decoratively; each color carries route or position meaning.
Do not reduce touch targets below 44 px or route-relevant mobile labels below 11 px.
